suite_result: 2 failed, 1206 passed, 10 skipped (python:3.13-slim via pytest_docker.sh). The 2 failures are test_seed_console.py::test_an_unreachable_erp_clears_nothing / ..._clears_no_crm_rows -- the known CRM_EMAIL/CRM_PASSWORD env dependency recorded in task 40.0 (stdout: 'CRM_BASE_URL, CRM_EMAIL and CRM_PASSWORD must be set'), unrelated to this change. test_crm_events_wiring.py all green.

findings.summary: With the switch on and Redis unreachable, every enqueue blocks the customer's thread ~1s, and 40.2 puts an ai_reply enqueue between consecutive sends of one reply -- so a Redis outage adds seconds per turn and a visible pause between a greeting and its buttons; crm_events has no go-offline switch like user_store's.
findings.failure: CRM_EVENTS_ENABLED=true, infra_redis unreachable (connect timeout). Customer taps a demo off the menu -> greeting is sent, then crm_events.outbound -> enqueue -> rpush waits the full 1s connect timeout, then the quick-question buttons go out 1.04s later; the whole turn takes 3.06s instead of 0.01s. Measured the same in a separate end-to-end probe (e2e/e2e_redis_down.py): switch off 0.01/0.01/0.01s per turn, switch on 2.03/3.06/2.03s, same 7 Meta sends either way. user_store, on the same Redis, trips its _go_offline breaker once and costs nothing after; crm_events retries the connect on every event. Outage-only and degraded-mode (events are lost anyway while Redis is down, which is accepted), hence P3; but 40.1's promise was that a down Redis 'must cost a second' -- 40.2 makes it cost one second per event, several per turn, on the thread the customer is waiting on.

self_check.spec_coverage: Every acceptance item in the 40.2 spec has a test in test_crm_events_wiring.py and I read each against the code: inbound body per type (text/image/image-bare/document/list/button/nfm/template button/sticker), BSUID-only sender phone=None, voice transcribed / failed / over-cap-not-transcribed / Meta retry pushed once and transcribed once, unidentifiable sender not pushed, ai_reply with Meta id + bot_id, menu bot_id None, send refused -> not pushed, 200-without-id -> WARNING not pushed, form fallback pushed, console_reply without bot_id, closing summary = ai_reply with bot_id, BSUID recipient, template push filed as our sentence, handover begin/console begin/renew/give back/menu end, repeat begin not pushed, end of nothing not pushed, expires_at = active_at + idle, four statuses + failed error code + unknown skipped + BSUID recipient + mixed webhook, both order sequences, switch-off whole conversation never builds a Redis client. The tests drive real paths (signed webhook, _handle_incoming_message send loop, console endpoints) and assert on queue contents read back, not on mocks of the code under test; the order tests would go red if customer_message moved after the send loop or touch lost its enqueue. Gaps: no test that a console reply Meta refuses is not pushed (code is right: outbound sits after send_message inside the try), and no test with Redis unavailable on the hot path (P3-1).

Conversation: hi -> pick Retail -> question -> same message again (Meta retry) -> 'can I speak to a human please' -> console reply -> console give back -> statuses webhook (delivered + failed 131047). Result: 16 events arrived in true order (customer_message, ai_reply[list] bot_id null, customer_message 'Retail', ai_reply greeting + ai_reply [buttons] bot_id retail, customer_message, ai_reply '*three*' (WhatsApp-formatted, i.e. what the customer saw), customer_message, handover_changed active expires +2h, ai_reply handover line, console_reply, handover_changed renewal, handover_changed inactive, delivery_status x2 with error_code 131047); retry deduped; every signature verified (0 rejected); queue 0, dead 0. A first run with WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN empty made every Meta send fail -- no ai_reply/console_reply was queued for any of them, which is the spec'd 'send failed -> not pushed' on real httpx. self_check.security: Nothing new. No secrets added (CRM_EVENTS_SECRET still env-only, default empty). Event bodies are conversation text already stored in the same Redis by user_store. AR-1/AR-2 unaffected by this change: nothing new committed that a public repo would leak.
self_check.spec_deviation: None without reason that I found. Files are the three listed plus crm_events.py, which the spec itself names for `outbound`. `_tell_crm` reads `handover_active_at` rather than active()'s `active_at or since` fallback, but every caller sets active_at first, so the fallback case cannot reach it. Notify pushes file `push.text` raw while the send-loop path files the WhatsApp-formatted, clipped payload text (so a console reply typed with **bold** shows as **bold** in the CRM but *bold* on the phone) -- matches the spec's 'notify 那段我们自己的文字', cosmetic, not reported. Pre-existing and not this task's: /console/reply calls touch even when the send failed, so a renewal is pushed with no console_reply beside it -- consistent with the chatbot's own takeover state, so not reported.

phase2.rebuttals: Mostly the defence holds; I checked its claims rather than its framing. (1) Self-decision 2, 'outbound is wrapped in try so an enqueue error can never turn a reply that went out into SEND_FAILED': true for exceptions, and the 'switch off = zero cost' half is true too (my e2e confirms no client is built). But it reasons only about exceptions, never about time: the failure mode a down Redis actually produces is a 1s blocking connect timeout, not a raise, and 40.2 placed that call between consecutive sends on the customer's thread. That is P3-1, and it is the one place the 'cannot hurt the customer's conversation' promise from 40.1 is not kept. (2) 'New tests were all green first time, so I distrusted them and ran three mutations': the mutations are real and I agree they bite (my reading of the order tests matches), but all of them, like all 37 tests, use a FakeRedis that only appends -- so the suite structurally cannot see anything Redis-shaped (latency, outage), which is exactly where the one finding sits. (3) 'Not verified: real phone, real CRM, live': accurate, but it skips a step that was cheap and that 40.1 did do, a local real-Redis + real-consumer + signature-checking receiver run of the wired paths. I did it (e2e/e2e_wiring.py): it passes, so the omission cost nothing this time, but the record presents unit tests with fakes as the whole verification. (4) Self-decisions 1, 3, 4, 5 (receipt occurred_at from Meta, profile-less reply uses `to`, [unknown]/[list_reply] fallbacks, handover occurred_at = enqueue time): all sound; 5 is also safe against the contract's 'older occurred_at is ignored' rule because begin/renew/end are second-granular and never reordered within one process. (5) Suite 1208 passed with CRM_EMAIL set matches my 1206 passed + the 2 known env failures.
phase2.blind_spot: Its 'known, not handled' list has three items: the gateway path pushing customer_message (accepted at batch level, I deliberately did not re-raise it), concurrent messages from one visitor not ordered (accepted in the edge-case section), and BSUID recipients addressed with `recipient` unverified against Meta. I noted the BSUID side only as 'recipient_user_id on statuses is a guess' in my e2e not-verified list; I did not separately call out that the outbound `recipient` key is itself unverified (whatsapp._recipient says so). So, a blind spot: I verified against our own code's assumptions about Meta's shapes (my stub Meta and my status payloads were written from the same assumptions), not against Meta. A self-consistent stub is a tautology at the boundary, the same trap the earlier rounds named. Conversely, it did not mention what I found, the outage latency, because every test and its reasoning lived inside a fake Redis that cannot time out.
